beats.narration_text: Bonjour. This is Liam, in for Bear. Which Claude model is the best? It's the natural question. But Anthropic's guide to choosing a model answers a different one. Which model is the right one for this job?

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A model: one version of Claude, like Sonnet or Opus. Autonomous: able to carry work forward on its own. And long-horizon: a task with many connected steps, from start to finish.

terms.meaning: one version of Claude, like Sonnet

a task with many connected steps

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Picture one best model, and every job goes to the same place. The quick question. The everyday draft. The hard problem. That's the picture the guide replaces.

shot.visual_intent: A grey figure ('you') at the left and one kraft file folder standing alone at the centre ('best?'); three task slips appear by the figure and fly one after another into the one folder as each job is named.

show.event: the draft and the hard problem go in

shot.motion_claim: A grey figure ('you') at the left and one kraft file folder standing alone at the centre ('best?'); three task slips appear by the figure and fly one after another into the one folder as each job is named.

beats.narration_text: Instead, it sorts four models by the kind of work they're for. Haiku, for instant answers. Sonnet, for everyday work. Opus, for specialized, complex tasks. And Fable, for your hardest work.

shot.visual_intent: The one folder slides to the right end of a row; its 'best?' label goes; three more folders slide in to its left, each with its tab one step further along, and each name lands beneath its folder as it is spoken ('Haiku', 'Sonnet', 'Opus', 'Fable').

show.event: the folder moves over; four slots

beats.narration_text: Haiku is the guide's most efficient model, for small, routine requests. Straightforward questions, simple summaries, quick lookups, pulling specific info out of text. Say you need one date from a long email. That's a Haiku job.

shot.visual_intent: A long email page appears above the figure ('email'); a small slip lifts off it ('one date') and is filed into the Haiku folder; the terracotta spark lands on Haiku's tab.
shot.motion_claim: A long email page appears above the figure ('email'); a small slip lifts off it ('one date') and is filed into the Haiku folder; the terracotta spark lands on Haiku's tab.

beats.narration_text: Sonnet, the guide says, is the versatile collaborator that can handle most problems. Writing and creating content, coding tasks, analysis and research, multi-step problems. Drafting a blog post. Fixing an ordinary bug. Sorting through survey answers.

shot.visual_intent: The spark moves from Haiku's tab to Sonnet's; three slips appear in a row above the figure and fly into the Sonnet folder one after another as each job is named.
shot.motion_claim: The spark moves from Haiku's tab to Sonnet's; three slips appear in a row above the figure and fly into the Sonnet folder one after another as each job is named.

beats.narration_text: When the problem is hard, Opus. The guide calls it the deep reasoning model for difficult problems. Complex research and analysis, long technical documents, methodology critique, agentic coding. Suppose you want the methods of a study picked apart, to see whether its conclusion holds.

shot.visual_intent: The spark moves to Opus's tab; a thick study (a stack of pages) appears above the figure ('a study'); a lens slides across it; the study shrinks and is filed into the Opus folder.
shot.motion_claim: The spark moves to Opus's tab; a thick study (a stack of pages) appears above the figure ('a study'); a lens slides across it; the study shrinks and is filed into the Opus folder.

beats.narration_text: And for your hardest work, Fable. The guide calls it the most autonomous model, for work that takes planning, not just reasoning. Long-horizon tasks with many connected steps. Dense source material. Building something from a rough idea.

shot.visual_intent: The spark moves to Fable's tab; a rough-idea slip appears ('rough idea'); a chain of five connected step tiles grows out of it ('many steps'); the whole chain gathers and is filed into the Fable folder.

show.event: planning: a chain of connected steps
a rough idea, filed under Fable

shot.motion_claim: The spark moves to Fable's tab; a rough-idea slip appears ('rough idea'); a chain of five connected step tiles grows out of it ('many steps'); the whole chain gathers and is filed into the Fable folder.

beats.narration_text: And one line on Fable's card is worth noticing. It's for problems that Opus struggled with. When a hard problem beats Opus, the guide points you one folder along.

shot.visual_intent: A slip rises out of the Opus folder, shakes above it, then crosses one folder along and drops into Fable.

show.event: it moves one folder along, to Fable

shot.motion_claim: A slip rises out of the Opus folder, shakes above it, then crosses one folder along and drops into Fable.

beats.narration_text: So how do you choose? Start from the job, not a leaderboard. Anthropic's developer docs describe two ways in. Start with an efficient model, and upgrade only if you need to. Or start with the strongest one for your task, and move down over time.

shot.visual_intent: A slip drops into Haiku, rises and steps up one folder at a time, with an ink arrow pointing up the row ('step up'); then a slip rises out of Opus and steps down to Sonnet, with an arrow pointing back ('step down').

show.event: start efficient; upgrade only if you need to
start strong; move down over time

shot.motion_claim: A slip drops into Haiku, rises and steps up one folder at a time, with an ink arrow pointing up the row ('step up'); then a slip rises out of Opus and steps down to Sonnet, with an arrow pointing back ('step down').

beats.narration_text: Either way, you make the call, one task at a time. There's no single best model. There's the right one for this job.

shot.visual_intent: A pointer glides in and clicks one folder's tab, and the spark lands there; a new slip goes from the figure into that folder; the figure is indicated ('you').

show.event: the right one for this job

shot.motion_claim: A pointer glides in and clicks one folder's tab, and the spark lands there; a new slip goes from the figure into that folder; the figure is indicated ('you').

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, with your own three tasks: Here are three things I need to do this week: task one, task two, task three. For each one, which Claude model fits, Haiku, Sonnet, Opus or Fable, and why? Then check two things yourself. If you can, run one task on the model it picked, and on one step smaller, and compare. And before you take its answer, ask yourself: was the task small and routine, everyday, deep reasoning, or long and many-step?
